title: One Ticket, 800 Years
summary: One Yellow Line ride through Delhi, Chandni Chowk to Qutab Minar, sweeps 800 years from Shah Jahan's 1639 city to 1199 and an older iron pillar, ending on a city that keeps being rebuilt.

fields.director_notes:
Who did what: MiniMax M3.1 flash via SandBase made every creative decision and wrote every line of the script; code only checks and executes. Claude Code wrote the open-source TimeLine tool, ran adversarial fact-check research, proposed the Yellow Line frame, pinned the title and word budget, and added the credit that some old-city blocks are illustrative. The maker chose Delhi, asked for a positive story and a male narrator, approved the custom voice, the 3D map and a painting per major stop, reviewed everything before upload and cut 6 claims; his 3 review notes went to the director, which rewrote those lines.
Pipeline: geo -> ground -> direct -> verify -> art -> assets -> timing -> render -> mix -> package.
Models/tools: MiniMax M3.1 flash, Speech 2.8 HD, Voice Design, Music 2.6; Google Nano Banana 2.1; OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Wikidata, Wikipedia, NASA Black Marble; three.js, playwright-core, ffmpeg.
Numbers: 19 director calls; 74 M3.1 requests ($0.43); media $1.19; total $1.61. 145 s, 12 scenes, 9 paintings; 24 claims (23 historical facts) checked against 39 sources, all supported after 3 repair rounds.
Code: https://github.com/Automationbot24x7/timeline-city
